Rashi on Eruvin 81a:11:1.hebrew: תפרה בקיסם - ככר שנפרסה, ותפר הפרוסות בקיסם, ונראית שלימה:
Rashi on Eruvin 81a:11:1.english: [If] one fastened it with a chip - A loaf that was broken, and [one] fastened the pieces with a chip, and it appears whole.

Rashi on Eruvin 81a:11:2.hebrew: ידיע תיפרה - ניכר מקום תפירתה, והויא כפרוסה:
Rashi on Eruvin 81a:11:2.english: Its seam is noticeable - The place of its stitching is noticeable, and it is [considered] like a broken piece.

Rashi on Eruvin 81a:14:1.hebrew: דשאר מיני הוה - מינין הרבה היו מעורבין בה, דההיא ודאי לאו פת היא, דכתיב גבי יחזקאל: ״ואתה קח לך חטין וגו'״, וכתיב (שם כד): ״לחם אנשים לא תאכל״ — אלמא לאו לחם הוא:
Rashi on Eruvin 81a:14:1.english: That it was of other species - Many types were mixed into it, for that certainly is not bread, as it is written regarding Ezekiel: “Take for yourself wheat, etc.”, and it is written: “Bread of men you shall not eat” (ibid. 24) — which shows that it is not bread.

Rashi on Eruvin 81a:16:1.hebrew: ועוגת שעורים תאכלנה אמר רב חסדא - האי שעורים לאו דווקא, דהא שאר מינין טובא הוו בה, אלא: לשיעורין תאכלנה — במשקל, דרך רעבון ולא לשובע:
Rashi on Eruvin 81a:16:1.english: “And you shall eat it as barley cakes.” Rav Ḥisda said - This [mention of] “barley” is not literal, for behold, there were many other species in it; rather, you shall eat it in measured portions — by weight, in the manner of famine and not to satiety.

Rashi on Eruvin 81a:16:2.hebrew: עריבתה כעריבת שעורין - מגונה, ולא יפה כתיקון עריבת חטים, שמייפה תיקון העוגה — עגולה ונאה:
Rashi on Eruvin 81a:16:2.english: Its preparation [must be] like the preparation of barley - Crude, and not fine like the preparation of kneading wheat, where one beautifies the fashioning of the cake — round and handsome.

Rashi on Eruvin 81a:17:1.english: A person may give a ma’a to a grocer - Who sells wine and resides with him in the alleyway.

Rashi on Eruvin 81a:17:2.hebrew: או לנחתום - מוכר ככרות, ודר עמו בחצר, שיזכה לו בעירוב עם חבריו: אם יבואו בני המבוי לקחת ממך ככר לעירוב או יין לשיתוף — יהא לי חלק בו:
Rashi on Eruvin 81a:17:2.english: Or to a baker - A seller of loaves, and he lives with him in the courtyard, so that he may confer possession upon him in an eiruv with his fellows: "If the residents of the alleyway come to take from you a loaf for an eiruv or wine for a shituf, let me have a share in it."

Rashi on Eruvin 81a:18:1.hebrew: לא זכו לו מעותיו - שאין מעות קונות עד שימשוך. ואפי' עירב החנוני הזה לכל האחרים וזיכה גם לזה — אינו עירוב; שהרי לא נתכוון לזכות לו במתנת חנם כשאר מזכין בעירוב, אלא לקנות המעה, והרי אינה קנויה לו, דכיון דמעות אינן קונות — לא סמכה דעתיה דהאי, ולא הוי דעתיה לאקנויי; ונמצא מערב לו במעותיו שלא מדעתו:
Rashi on Eruvin 81a:18:1.english: His money did not confer possession on him - For money does not effect an acquisition until one pulls [the merchandise]. And even if this grocer established an eiruv for all the others and conferred possession upon this [person] as well, it is not an eiruv; for he did not intend to confer possession upon him as a free gift like others who confer possession for an eiruv, but rather to acquire the ma’ah, yet it is not acquired by him. For since money does not effect an acquisition, this one’s mind was not at ease and [the grocer’s] intention was not to transfer ownership; and it turns out that he establishes an eiruv for him with his money without his consent.

Rashi on Eruvin 81a:2:1.hebrew: לאפוקי מדר' יהושע דאמר פת אין מידי אחרינא לא קא משמע לן מתני' בכל - אפילו יין ופירות. ואי מההיא, הוה אמינא: התם הוא דבעירובי תחומין עסקינן, והתם מודה רבי יהושע דליכא למיחש משום איבה כי הכא בעירובי חצירות, דטעמא משום איבה כדלקמן, אבל בעירובי חצירות אימא לא; להכי הדר תנייה גבי חצירות. לישנא אחרינא גרסינן: לאפוקי מדר' מאיר דאמר: בפת אין, במידי אחרינא לא — בפרק הדר (לעיל עירובין דף עא:) — קמ"ל בכל; והיא היא:
Rashi on Eruvin 81a:2:1.english: To exclude [the opinion] of Rabbi Yehoshua, who said: Bread, yes; anything else, no; the mishna teaches us "with all" - Even wine and fruit. And if [we were to deduce this only] from that [earlier mishna], I would have said: It is [specifically] there, where we are dealing with eiruvei techumin, and there Rabbi Yehoshua concedes, since there is no concern for enmity as there is here with eiruvei chatzerot, where the reason [for requiring bread] is due to enmity, as [explained] below; but with eiruvei chatzerot, say [that] no [other food is valid, only bread]! Therefore, [the mishna] repeated it regarding [eiruvei] courtyards. Another version reads: "To exclude [the opinion] of Rabbi Meir, who said: With bread, yes; with anything else, no — in the chapter [entitled] Hadar (above, Eruvin 71b) — [the mishna] teaches us 'with all'"; and it is the very same [reasoning].

Rashi on Eruvin 81a:3:1.hebrew: איתיביה אביי בכל מערבין עירובי חצירות גרסינן ובכל משתתפין שיתופי מבוי - בין בפת, ובין ביין, בין בשאר פירות:
Rashi on Eruvin 81a:3:1.english: Abaye raised an objection: One may establish a joining of courtyards with all [kinds of food] — this is our reading — and one may establish a merging of alleyways with all [kinds of food] - Whether with bread, or with wine, or with other produce.

Rashi on Eruvin 81a:3:2.hebrew: ולא אמרו לערב בפת כו' - ובכל מערבין דרישא, הכי קאמר: בכל מיני פת מערבין עירובי חצירות:
Rashi on Eruvin 81a:3:2.english: And they only said to establish an eiruv with bread, etc. - And [regarding] “with all [things] one may establish an eiruv” in the opening clause, this is what it means: With all types of bread one may establish an eiruv of courtyards.

Rashi on Eruvin 81a:3:3.hebrew: מאן שמעת ליה דאמר פת אין מידי אחרינא לא רבי יהושע - וללישנא אחרינא, ר' מאיר:
Rashi on Eruvin 81a:3:3.english: Who did you hear that said [that with] bread, yes, [but with] anything else, no? Rabbi Yehoshua - And according to the other version, [it is] Rabbi Meir.

Rashi on Eruvin 81a:3:4.hebrew: וקתני בכל - אפת. ומתניתין נמי, ממאי דבכל דתני אכל מילי קאמר, ולאפוקי מהא דר' יהושע אתא? דילמא בכל דקתני — אפת קאי, כברייתא, והכי קאמר: בכל מיני פת מערבין בחצירות, ומשתתפין במבוי בכל מילי, חוץ ממים ומלח:
Rashi on Eruvin 81a:3:4.english: And it teaches: “With all” - [This refers] to bread. And [regarding] our Mishnah as well: From where [is it known] that the “with all” that it teaches means regarding all things, and that it comes to exclude this [opinion] of Rabbi Yehoshua? Perhaps the “with all” that it teaches refers to bread, like the baraita, and this is what it means: With all kinds of bread one may establish an eiruv in courtyards, and one may merge in an alleyway with all things, except for water and salt.

Rashi on Eruvin 81a:4:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רבה בר בר חנה - אי איכא למימר דאפקא מתני' מדרבי יהושע, אסיפא דמלתא פליגא, דאמר ״פרוסה לא״ — קא משמע לן ״בכל״:
Rashi on Eruvin 81a:4:1.english: Rather, Rabba bar bar Ḥana said - If it can be said that the Mishnah excludes [the view] of Rabbi Yehoshua, it disputes the end of his statement, where he said [that] a broken loaf [is] not [valid] — [hence, the Mishnah] teaches us: "With all."

Rashi on Eruvin 81a:5:1.hebrew: משום איבה - שבאין לידי מחלוקת, שאומר: ״אני נותן שלימה, ואתה פרוסה״:
Rashi on Eruvin 81a:5:1.english: Due to enmity - For they will come to dispute, as [one] says: "I am giving a whole [loaf], and you [are giving] a slice."

Rashi on Eruvin 81a:6:1.english: To its corrupted state - [Where] this one [gives] a broken [loaf] and that one a whole [loaf].

Rashi on Eruvin 81a:7:1.english: Its ḥalla - It is not [considered] a deficiency, as this is its rectification.

Rashi on Eruvin 81a:8:1.hebrew: כדי דימועה - אם נדמעת, שנפלה תרומה בחולין ועשו ממנה ככר זו, ונטלו ממנה דימועה — אחד ממאה — לתקנה:
Rashi on Eruvin 81a:8:1.english: As much as its dimua - If it became mixed [with teruma], in that teruma fell into non-sacred produce and they made this loaf from it, and they removed its dimua portion from it — one out of a hundred — to rectify it.

Rashi on Eruvin 81a:9:1.hebrew: חלת נחתום - קטנה היא, ואין זה חסרון:
Rashi on Eruvin 81a:9:1.english: A baker’s ḥalla - It is small, and this is not [considered] a deficiency.

Tosafot on Eruvin 81a:13:1.hebrew: והא ההיא דהואי בשני דמר שמואל כו' - עשו לנסות מה טעמא, לפי שצוה הקב"ה ליחזקאל לעשות:
Tosafot on Eruvin 81a:13:1.english: "But there was that [bread] in the days of Mar Shmuel, etc." - They made [it] to test what its taste was, because the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded Ezekiel to make [it].

Tosafot on Eruvin 81a:14:1.hebrew: דכתיב ואתה קח לך כו' - פ"ה: וכתיב בתריה "לחם אנשים לא תאכל", אלמא לאו לחם הוא. והגיה ר"ת, דהאי "לחם אנשים" בהבראה כתיב, רחוק מפרשה זו כמה דפין. והכי פירושא: "ההיא דשאר מינין הואי, דכתיב: ואתה קח לך" — ולימי המצור ושעת הדחק נאכל, ולא פת הוא אלא לנפש רעבה, ד"כלבא בכפניה גלליה בלע" [ב"ק צב:]:
Tosafot on Eruvin 81a:14:1.english: "As it is written: 'And you, take for yourself...'" etc. - Rashi explained: And it is written after it, "You shall not eat the bread of men" [Ezekiel 24:17], which shows that it is not [considered] bread. But Rabbeinu Tam emended [this]: For this [verse], "the bread of men," is written regarding the meal of condolence, several pages away from this passage. And this is the explanation [of the Gemara]: "That [bread] was of other species [mixed together], as it is written: 'And you, take for yourself...'" — and it was eaten [only] for the days of siege and a time of distress, and it is not [considered] bread except for a ravenous soul, for "a dog in its hunger swallows [even] its own excrement" [Bava Kamma 92b].

Tosafot on Eruvin 81a:18:1.hebrew: לא זכו לו מעותיו - פירש הקונטרס: "ואפילו עירב החנוני הוה לכל האחרים וזכה גם לזה — אינו עירוב, שהרי לא נתכוון לזכות לו במתנת חנם כשאר מזכין בעירוב, אלא לקנות המעה, והרי אינה קנויה לו". ובחנם פירש כן, דאפילו מתכוין לו להקנות לו בחנם, ואפילו זיכה לו ע"י אחר, או לקח המעה וקנה לו מן השוק — אינו עירוב; כיון שהנותן מתכוין לקנות לו מן החנוני, ואין המעה קונה לו, וכל הזכיות שעושה החנוני — של מדעת בעל הבית קא עביד, ואין מערבין אלא לדעתו. ולשון הקונטרס נמי מוכיח כן בסמוך:
Tosafot on Eruvin 81a:18:1.english: His money did not confer possession on him - Rashi explained: "And even if the grocer established an eiruv for all the others and conferred possession upon this [person] as well, it is not a valid eiruv, because he did not intend to confer possession upon him as a free gift like others who confer possession for an eiruv, but rather to acquire the ma’a, and it is not acquired by him." And he explained this without need, for even if [the grocer] intended to transfer [ownership] to him for free, and even if he conferred possession upon him via another [person], or [the grocer] took the ma’a and bought [food] for him from the marketplace, it is not a valid eiruv; since the one giving [the coin] intends to buy [food] for himself from the grocer, and the ma’a does not acquire [it] for him, and all the acts of conferring possession that the grocer performs, he is doing without the homeowner’s consent, and one may establish an eiruv [for a person] only with his consent. And the phrasing of Rashi nearby also proves this.

Tosafot on Eruvin 81a:3:1.hebrew: איתיביה אביי בכל מערבין עירובי תחומין כו' - כך היא הגירסא בספרים ישנים, וכן גרס ר"ח. ופירש ה"ר אברהם כולה סוגיא, דה"ק: "תנינא חדא זימנא בכל מערבין כו'" — משמע סתמא: בין בעירובי חצירות בין בעירובי תחומין. "אמר רבה: לאפוקי מר' יהושע דאמר פת אין כו'" — והאי "בכל מערבין" אכולהו עירובין קאי, ואכולהו פליג ר' יהושע ואומר: פת — אין, מידי אחרינא — לא. ולהכי איצטריך תרי זימני: דאי לא הדר ותנא בבא דהכא, הוה מוקמינן ההיא דלעיל בתחומין, דאיירי בהו כולי פירקא, ומילתא דר' יהושע דהכא הוה מוקמינן בחצירות, דמיירי בהו לעיל, ולא מפקא ההיא דלעיל כלל מרבי יהושע דהכא; אבל השתא דמיתניא נמי גבי מלתיה דרבי יהושע, מפקא מדידיה, דלאיפלוגי קאתי. "איתיביה אביי" — אביי פריך על מה שאמר שסבר רבי יהושע דאפילו בתחומין אין מערבין אלא בפת; והכי גרסינן בכל הספרים הישנים: "בכל מערבין עירובי תחומין". קאמר כו' — קס"ד דהאי "בכל מערבין", בכל מיני פירות קאמר: "מאן שמעת ליה דאמר פת אין מידי אחרינא לא? רבי יהושע", דהא אמרינן דר' אליעזר "בכל מערבין" בין בחצירות בין בתחומין קאמר, וקתני לה גבי תחומין "בכל דבר", אלמא תחומין בכל דבר לרבי יהושע. "אלא לאפוקי מרבי יהושע כו'" — אלא האי "בכל מערבין" ה"ק: בכל עניני פת מערבין, בין בשלמין בין בחסרין; והשתא מיירי מתני' "בכל מערבין" דווקא בחצירות דאיירי בהו לעיל, ופליג על ר' יהושע דבעי שלמין בחצירות. והא דלא שני אפירכא דאביי דודאי רבי יהושע מודה דתחומין בכל דבר, ובמתניתין תנן "בכל מערבין" אפילו בחצירות, ור' יהושע פליג בחצירות לחודייהו — היינו משום דאי ר' אליעזר איירי בתרוייהו ור' יהושע לא פליג אלא אחצירות, הוה ליה לפרושי דאחצירות לחודייהו קאי:
Tosafot on Eruvin 81a:3:1.english: "Abaye raised an objection: One may establish an eiruv with all [kinds of food], an eiruv of Shabbat boundaries, etc." - Such is the reading in old books, and so Rabbeinu Chananel read. And Harav Rabbi Avraham explained the entire sugya, that this is what it is saying: "We have [already] learned [it] once: 'One may establish an eiruv with all [kinds of food]...'" — this implies generically: whether regarding eiruvei chatzeirot or regarding eiruvei techumin. "Rabba said: To exclude [the opinion of] Rabbi Yehoshua, who said: Bread, yes, etc." — and this [ruling,] "One may establish an eiruv with all [kinds of food]," applies to all eiruvin, and Rabbi Yehoshua disputes all of them and says: Bread, yes; anything else, no. And for this [reason] it was necessary [to teach it] twice: For had [the Mishnah] not repeated and taught the clause here, we would have established that [mishnah] above as [referring to] techumin, since the entire chapter deals with them, and Rabbi Yehoshua's statement here we would have established as [referring to] chatzeirot, which [the Mishnah] dealt with previously, and that [mishnah] above would not exclude [the view of] Rabbi Yehoshua here at all. But now that it is also taught next to Rabbi Yehoshua's statement, it excludes his [view], since it comes to dispute [him]. "Abaye raised an objection" — Abaye is objecting to what [Rabba] said, that Rabbi Yehoshua maintains that even for techumin one may only establish an eiruv with bread; and so we read in all the old books: "One may establish an eiruv with all [kinds of food], an eiruv of Shabbat boundaries." [When the Gemara] says "etc." — it assumed that this [phrase], "One may establish an eiruv with all [kinds of food]," means with all kinds of fruit: "Who did you hear who said that bread, yes, but anything else, no? Rabbi Yehoshua." For we say that Rabbi Eliezer's [statement], "One may establish an eiruv with all [kinds of food]," was said both regarding chatzeirot and regarding techumin, and [the baraita] teaches with regard to techumin "with all things" — evidently [an eiruv of] techumin may be [made] with all things according to Rabbi Yehoshua! [Therefore, the Gemara rejects Rabba's explanation and states:] "Rather, to exclude [the opinion of] Rabbi Yehoshua, etc." — rather, this [phrase], "One may establish an eiruv with all [kinds of food]," this is what it is saying: With all types of bread one may establish an eiruv, whether whole or broken; and now, the Mishnah's [ruling], "One may establish an eiruv with all [kinds of food]," deals specifically with chatzeirot, which [the Mishnah] dealt with previously, and it disputes Rabbi Yehoshua, who requires whole [loaves] for chatzeirot. And as for [the question of] why [the Gemara] did not answer Abaye's objection [by saying] that Rabbi Yehoshua certainly concedes that techumin [may be established] with all things, and in the Mishnah we learned "One may establish an eiruv with all [kinds of food]" even for chatzeirot, and Rabbi Yehoshua disputes only regarding chatzeirot — that is because if Rabbi Eliezer was speaking of both [types of eiruv] and Rabbi Yehoshua disputed only regarding chatzeirot, [Rabbi Yehoshua] should have specified that he refers to chatzeirot alone.

Tosafot on Eruvin 81a:7:1.hebrew: כדי חלתה וכדי דימועה מערבין לו בה - ונראה לר"י: דווקא בטבולה לחלה ובמדומע איירי, דאי לא בעיא תיקון — איכא איבה אפילו בחסרון מועט, דלישנא דמתניתין משמע דשלמים לגמרי בעי. ומיהו, לשון "כדי" קשה, דהוה ליה למימר "חלתה ודמועתה"! ואור"י: דנקט "כדי" לאשמועינן, דאפילו נטל לשם חלה, אם הפריש יותר מכדי צורך — איכא איבה. ואם תאמר: כיון דאשמעינן כדי חלתה, דהוה אחד מארבעים ושמונה — כל שכן כדי דימועה, דהוה יותר ממאה? ואור"י: דס"ד דדימוע, כיון דחזי הכי לכהן — אפילו בפורתא איכא איבה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 81a:7:1.english: "As much as its ḥalla and as much as its mixture, they may establish an eiruv for him with it" - And it appears to the Ri that [the Gemara] is dealing specifically with [a loaf that was] untithed for ḥalla [tevolah le-ḥalla] and with a mixture [of teruma and non-sacred bread, meduma], for if it did not require rectification, there is animosity even with a slight deficiency, as the language of the Mishnah implies that it requires completely whole [loaves]. However, the phrasing "as much as" [kedei] is difficult, for it should have said: "its ḥalla and its mixture"! And the Ri says that it used [the term] "as much as" to teach us that even if one took [a portion] for the sake of ḥalla, if he separated more than the necessary amount, there is animosity. And if you say: Since it taught us "as much as its ḥalla," which is one forty-eighth, all the more so [is it permitted with] "as much as its mixture," which is [one part in] more than a hundred? And the Ri says: For it might have entered your mind [to say] that regarding a mixture, since it is fit as is for a priest, even with a slight [deficiency] there is animosity.
